title: Timeline Infographic Templates: 20 Designs You Can Customize for Free
excerpt: Find the right timeline infographic template for your project — 20 free, editable designs for history timelines, roadmaps, and project milestones.
html:
A timeline infographic template solves one of the hardest problems in data storytelling: making time look like a journey rather than a list of dates. Whether you're presenting a company history slide, a product launch roadmap, or historical milestones, the layout has to show progression. Get it right and the narrative flow feels natural. Get it wrong and you've built a list of text blocks that readers have to scroll through to understand the timeline. This guide covers the main timeline formats, customization rules, and where to download 20 free editable templates.

Why Timeline Layouts Succeed or Fail

Time is linear, but timeline designs don't have to be. The most common mistake in timeline infographic design is using a vertical layout when a horizontal flow fits the screen better — or vice-versa.

The rules of timeline direction:

* Horizontal timelines work best on slides, presentations, and widescreen monitors (16:9 aspect ratio). They read left-to-right, matching how Western audiences scan pages. Keep the step count to six or fewer to prevent crowding.

* Vertical timelines work best on mobile screens, blog posts, and vertical infographics. They scroll naturally and can handle more milestones (up to 10–12 dates) because the page can expand downward indefinitely.

The second point of failure is inconsistent date spacing. A timeline where the gap between 2020 and 2021 is the same size as the gap between 2021 and 2025 misleads the eye. If the timeline is scaled by actual duration, space the milestones proportionally. If you are comparing milestones rather than showing duration, use a step-by-step layout instead.

The 20 Templates, Sized for Every Platform

This collection includes 20 free editable timeline templates built for Canva, Figma, and PowerPoint:

* Company History Timelines — 5 templates featuring vertical tracks with alternating text blocks and image placeholders.

* Product Roadmaps & Launch Plans — 5 templates using horizontal Gantt-style bars to show overlapping phases.

* Project Milestone Sliders — 5 widescreen templates for PowerPoint slides, designed for quick scanning in meetings.

* Historical Event Timelines — 5 vertical layouts with high-density annotation fields for detailed stories.

All 20 templates are free to use and fully customizable with your brand assets.

How to Customize a Timeline Template

The most common mistake when customizing a timeline is trying to fit too much text into each milestone. If a date block has room for 10 words and you paste 40, the text wraps, the line spacing breaks, and the timeline looks cluttered.

To customize successfully, edit your copy to fit the placeholder size. Keep milestone headers short (2–4 words) and body descriptions under 15 words. Let the dates and icons carry the chronological story.

In Canva, use the "align" feature to ensure all date dots and line connectors sit on the same horizontal or vertical axis. In Figma, auto-layout will maintain consistent spacing between milestones automatically as you add text. If your timeline requires custom date proportional spacing, sketch the axis line first, place the milestone dots, and then add text blocks.

One design tip: use a single accent color for the "current" milestone or the most important date on the timeline, and gray or muted brand colors for everything else. This tells the reader where the story is heading.

Time-based data needs structure to become a story. Use these 20 free timeline infographic templates to map your milestones and launch plans with confidence. See our Chart Types Guide for help matching your data to the right format.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a timeline infographic?

A timeline infographic is a visual layout that displays events, milestones, or project phases in chronological order. It uses a horizontal or vertical axis line, milestone markers (like dots or icons), dates, and short text descriptions to show progression over time. It is highly effective for history presentations, roadmaps, and project planning.

How do I make a timeline infographic for free?

Canva is the easiest starting point — search "timeline infographic" in the template library to browse hundreds of free layouts you can customize in your browser. Figma Community also offers free templates for designers who want custom auto-layout grids. All 20 templates in the IllustrateWords gallery are free to download and edit.

What size should a timeline infographic be?

For presentations and monitors: 1920 × 1080px (16:9 widescreen). For mobile screens and social media: 1080 × 1350px or 1080 × 1920px. For web page embeds: 800 × 1200px or taller for vertical scroll layouts. Design your timeline at 2× resolution if possible to keep dates and connector lines crisp.

When should I use a horizontal timeline instead of a vertical one?

Use a horizontal timeline when presenting on a screen, monitor, or slide deck where space is wider than it is tall. Use a vertical timeline for blogs, landing pages, and mobile viewports where readers scroll vertically. Vertical timelines are also better when you have more than 6 milestones.

How many milestones should a timeline have?

Keep horizontal timelines to 4–6 milestones to maintain readability on a screen. Vertical timelines can handle 8–12 milestones because the scroll length is flexible. If you have more events than that, group them into years or phases rather than displaying every date individually.
